gaps.sentence: The museum’s guiding ___ is that admission should be free.
gaps.explanation: 'Principle' = a guiding rule or belief; 'principal' means main or head person.

gaps.sentence: It would be ___ to take an umbrella — the sky is black.
gaps.explanation: 'Sensible' means showing good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected by things or feelings.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: Smoke could be seen ___ from the factory chimneys.
gaps.hint: the smoke goes up by itself — no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (no object) describes the smoke going up; 'raise' would need an object (raise something).

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her presentation and her handling of questions.
The wine is the perfect ___ to the meal.
gaps.explanation: 'Complement' = something that completes or goes well with; 'compliment' is praise.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.
